profiles.name: Anton Prushchuk
profiles.description:
Anton Prushchuk was born 1898 in Brest-Litovsk, Russia (present-day Belarus). Immigrated to the United States in 1913.

Immigrated to the United States in 1913 to avoid military service. Worked in Detroit and was probably a member of the Union of Russian Workers, though he denied it. An avowed pacifist, he was arrested in 1918 for failing to register for the draft and illegally inducted into the US Army. Court-martialed in June 1918 for refusing orders, he was sentenced to five years’ imprisonment and confined at the Fort Leavenworth Disciplinary Barracks and later Fort Douglas, Utah, until August 1919, when he was dishonorably discharged. Arrested again during the second Palmer Raids in November 1919 and deported to Poland January 22, 1921. 

Arrested by the Soviet government due to his anarchism, he participated in a hunger strike in Petrograd’s House of Preliminary Detention in November 1922 and was force-fed through a catheter.

Adapted from Kenyon Zimmer, Red Scare Deportees (kenyonzimmer.com), compiled from INS deportation case files.

profiles.description:
Demian Vlasov was born 1893 in Kyiv, Russia (present-day Ukraine). Immigrated to the United States in 1912.

Deported to Russia, January 22, 1921. No further information found.

INS file 54709/104; FBI file OG 369065

profiles.name: Emil Feltman
profiles.description:
Emil Feltman was born 1881. Immigrated to the United States in 1882.

Migrated to the United States as an infant with his father; orphaned by age six following his father’s death in a mining accident in Butte, Montana. Enlisted in the US Army in 1898 and served in the Spanish-American and Philippine-American wars; honorably discharged in 1900. Joined the IWW in 1913 and became an organizer in 1918. Married fellow IWW member Fannie Martini in Bisbee, Arizona, in 1916. Arrested in Jerome, Arizona, in February 1919 while organizing miners during a strike. According to the arresting officer, “he also said that it didn’t make any difference where he was deported to, whether it was Germany or China, he would continue his present agitation as organizer of the I.W.W.s.” His mental and physical health deteriorated while detained. Deported on May 22, 1920.

After deportation, worked briefly as a coal miner in Westphalia and later migrated to Soviet Russia, becoming one of the first Americans to join the Kuzbas Autonomous Industrial Colony in Siberia. Left Russia along with sixteen other disillusioned Kuzbas members in September 1922.

Adapted from Kenyon Zimmer, Red Scare Deportees (kenyonzimmer.com), compiled from INS deportation case files.

profiles.name: Ernest Emil Albert Heitmiller
profiles.description:
Ernest Emil Albert Heitmiller was born 1887 in Linden-Limmer, Germany. Immigrated to the United States in 1914.

Entered the United States in 1914 via Canada without inspection. Worked as a sailor and lumber worker and became active in the Industrial Workers of the World, eventually serving as a delegate and organizer. Arrested in Seattle in February 1919 and deported on January 7, 1920.

He afterward wrote of his experiences as a passenger aboard the SS Mongolia: “It was a bad trip, as the ship had no accommodations for the many passengers…Several died on the journey and it is a wonder that no contagious sickness developed.”

profiles.name: Erofey Okoletenko
profiles.description:
Erofey Okoletenko was born 1895 in Kyiv, Russia (present-day Ukraine). Immigrated to the United States in 1914.

Joined the URW in Detroit in 1916. Arrested January 21, 1919 following a jail term for “disorderly conduct and loitering,” he escaped custody June 5, 1920 but later surrendered at Ellis Island on the advice of attorney Isaac Shorr. He was deported February 1, 1921, supplied by the U.S. government with a fraudulent passport issued by the anti-Communist Ukrainian Diplomatic Mission. 

In 1923 he traveled to Mexico and reentered the United States, where he was arrested for illegal entry. In 1924 he was again deported via Switzerland, but was turned away at the Russian border and returned to the U.S. ON August 23, 1924 he was deported once more, and returned to U.S. again in September 1924 after being not being permitted to enter Switzerland. Finally he was “paroled in his own custody” (i.e. set free).

Adapted from Kenyon Zimmer, Red Scare Deportees (kenyonzimmer.com), compiled from INS deportation case files.

profiles.name: George Schwartzwalder
profiles.description:
George Schwartzwalder was born 1882 in Baden, Germany. Immigrated to the United States in 1910.

George Schwartzwalder migrated repeatedly across Europe in his youth, living in Austria, Russia, and Italy before returning to Germany, where he served three years in the army and later worked as a sailor between Germany and Argentina.

Immigrated to the United States in 1910 and lived as a migrant laborer. Although sympathetic to the Industrial Workers of the World since 1915, he formally joined the organization only in December 1918 in Kansas City. He was also a personal friend of Joe Hill. Classified as an “enemy alien” during World War I, he was arrested in Bartlesville in February 1919 and interrogated for five hours before being released, then arrested again the following month in Muskogee, Oklahoma, where he lost thirty to forty pounds in unsanitary jail conditions. He told officials he hated the Kaiser because “he represented the capitalist class in Germany” and declared “he would not fight for any country, that he felt no patriotism for any country.” Deported to Germany January 7, 1920.

Adapted from Kenyon Zimmer, Red Scare Deportees (kenyonzimmer.com), compiled from INS deportation case files.

William Milligan was born 1874 in Edinburgh, Scotland. Worked as a miner.

Migrated to South Africa c. 1900, then to Australia and Mexico, before arriving in the United States around 1901.
